widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
- <Subject 1>: The exact car from <Image 1>: its body shape, proportions, color, materials, wheels, windows, badges and any visible details. Preserve proportions, colors, materials and identity exactly in every frame.
- <Subject 2>: The same driving environment from <Video 1>, including the road, the surroundings, the weather, the lighting and the camera vantage - photoreal, unchanged.
- <Subject 3>: The source performance from <Video 1>: the Mercedes's driving motion - its path, speed profile, steering behavior, lane position, and the overall timing of the drive.
- <Image 1>: The car reference image used as the full appearance anchor for <Subject 1>.
- <Video 1>: The source video used as the reference for the camera (its movement and vantage), the environment, the weather, the lighting, the atmosphere, and the driving motion to be preserved.

summary:
video editing + reference generation. Replace the Mercedes in <Video 1> with the car <Subject 1> from <Image 1> for the ENTIRE video - the car is present from the very first frame and stays throughout; the Mercedes never appears in any frame, including the opening. Preserve the camera movement, the environment, the weather, the lighting, the atmosphere, the driving path, the speed and the overall timing. The car follows exactly where the Mercedes drove, adapted to its dimensions.

retention_analysis:
- <Image 1> - fully_preserved: preserve the car's body shape, proportions, color, materials, wheels, windows, badges and details, to pixel level in every frame.
- <Video 1> - partially_preserved: preserve the camera (its movement and vantage), the environment (road, surroundings), the weather, the lighting, the atmosphere, and the driving trajectory and timing; remove the Mercedes's body from EVERY frame and replace it with <Subject 1>.
- <Subject 1> - fully_preserved: retain the car's identity, proportions, color, materials and all details, identical to <Image 1> in every frame.
- <Subject 2> - fully_preserved: retain the road, surroundings, weather, lighting and camera, photoreal, unchanged.
- <Subject 3> - attribute_transfer: transfer the driving path, lane position, speed profile, steering behavior and timing onto the car, adapting to its dimensions and handling so it occupies the same road position and follows the same trajectory.

detailed_description:
Create a seamless photorealistic car-replacement edit. The car must appear physically present in the original footage with correct scale, perspective, weight, contact with the road, reflections on its body matching the environment, and shadows - no distortion, no warping, no floating. The drive follows <Video 1>'s path, speed and timing: the car stays in the same lane, follows the same trajectory and speed, and arrives at the same positions at the same moments as the Mercedes did, adapted to its own dimensions. The camera, environment, weather, lighting and atmosphere stay photoreal exactly as in <Video 1>, unchanged.

overall_soundscape:
Identical to <Video 1> except the engine note is adapted to the new car - an appropriate engine sound replacing the Mercedes's - with road, traffic and ambience unchanged.

non_diegetic_music:
Kept identical to <Video 1>.
